source.title: Maximum Side Length of a Square with Sum Less than or Equal to Threshold

teaching.hint: How does removing rows and columns from a qualifying square affect its sum?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Nonnegative entries make feasible square sizes downward closed; repeated square-sum queries can share a 2D cumulative-sum table.
solution_outline.approach: Build 2D prefix sums. For a proposed positive side length, inspect every square placement using an inclusion-exclusion sum query. Binary-search for the greatest side with any qualifying placement, treating side zero as the fallback.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The feasibility test checks all squares of one side exactly; the search retains the largest feasible side in its interval, with zero allowed when no positive side works.
solution_outline.correctness: Inclusion-exclusion gives each candidate square its exact sum. Any valid larger square contains a smaller square with no greater sum, so feasible sizes form a prefix. The complete placement test and a greatest-feasible boundary search therefore return exactly the largest permitted side.
solution_outline.complexity: O(mn log(min(m,n)+1)) time and O(mn) space.
solution_outline.pitfall: The size predicate would not be monotone if negative entries were allowed.

common_wrong_turns: The size predicate would not be monotone if negative entries were allowed.
source_fidelity_notes: Restated the square as consecutive rows and columns so diagrams are unnecessary; kept nonnegative values. Used the complete primary binary-search route, not the underexplained alternative.
